output.evidence: Version 2 executes the Chartreuse Hard-Edge Paradox far more completely: the dark solid triangle is a real hard-edge gouache shape whose base sinks under the flacon and whose apex rises behind the cap, while the cream outline triangle offsets out from behind it on the right, keeping the parallel-hypotenuse paradox legible. Its top band matches the brief's hierarchy better: minimal tracked PRADA at very top, a much larger single-line Bodoni 'Paradoxe' approaching full width, and a thin near-full-width ink-green registration rule beneath it, all on a flat shadowless chartreuse field with the matte card swallowing light so the peach juice and black lacquer cap own the highlights. Version 1 by comparison reduces the solid triangle to a thin sliver under the base that reads as a cast shadow rather than a graphic solid, keeps the outline triangle small and clipped at the lower right so the paradox barely registers, and sets the title at roughly half width with a short centered rule, leaving thetop band under-scaled and the hierarchy unresolved. Both keep the product faithful and centered in the lower field with no studio equipment or floating-support artifacts, but version 2 is the stronger finished poster within this concept.
remaining_problems: In version 2 the title line and the registration rule are left-weighted rather than truly centered across the full width, slightly undercutting the quiet symmetric top band the brief calls for.
The outline triangle's hypotenuse is largely occluded by the cap and shoulder, so the 'parallel but never intersecting' paradox reads only partially.
The solid dark triangle's apex emerges beside the cap as a small stray wedge at upper right, a minor hard-edge registration slip against the otherwise clean silhouette.
Baked-in speculars on the black cap still imply the original softbox setup rather than the declared flat frontal ink light, though the matte field largely absorbs the mismatch.
